title: South African Chenin
subtitle: Old vines and new energy
objectives: Explain the role of old vines

steps.title: Styles
steps.body: South African Chenin ranges from crisp, fruity, unoaked wines with tropical and apple notes to rich, oaked, textured wines from old vines. The Chenin Blanc Association classifies styles: fresh and fruity, rich and ripe unwooded, rich and ripe wooded, and rich and ripe sweet.
steps.highlight: Fresh to rich, unoaked to oaked

steps.title: Old vines
steps.body: Many South African Chenin vineyards are old, dry-farmed bush vines, some planted in the 1960s and earlier. The Old Vine Project certifies vineyards over 35 years. Swartland, with granite and schist soils, became the centre of a revival from the early 2000s, led by producers like Eben Sadie and Chris and Andrea Mullineux.

steps.prompt: Which South African region led the Chenin revival from the early 2000s?
steps.explanation: Swartland's old bush vines and young producers drove the revival.

steps.title: Why it suits the Cape
steps.body: Chenin's high acidity is valuable in the Cape's warm climate, keeping wines fresh as they ripen fully. Old bush vines, deep-rooted, cope with drought without irrigation. The result is concentrated wine with acidity, giving South Africa a world-class white style of its own.

steps.prompt: What makes old-vine Chenin special in South Africa?
steps.explanation: Old vines give low, not high, yields.

steps.title: What you learned
points: South African Chenin ranges from fresh to rich and oaked
Old dry-farmed bush vines drive quality
Swartland led the revival from the early 2000s
